name: Prize crossword No 23,646
preamble: The opening words of a novel (2,2,1,5,11,12) are to go across the top of the perimeter and down the two sides, the two long words each extending round the corner into the bottom line, in the rest of which goes the local town where perplexed beginners abandon trigonometry (7). Remaining solutions are to go into the diagram jigsaw-wise, wherever they will go; their clues are listed in alphabetical order of the solutions, acrosses and downs being considered separately. Characters in the novel are asterisked. Please note the numbers on this grid should be ignored.

clue.text: I tend to keep company proceeding as planned

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
to tend a patient is to nurse them
CO is the standard abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Someone admits they tend to keep company with others, as long as things go to plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'tend to' as 'usually'; here 'tend' is a verb of its own, nursing, and wraps round the company.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in course is under way in the normal sequence, which is what proceeding as planned describes.

clue.text: Warning: signallers' letter's wrong

blocks.note: Toc was the old army signallers' word for the letter T
a sin is a moral wrong

explanation.surface: A warning that the signallers have got a letter wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Before the modern phonetic alphabet, British signallers said 'Toc' for T (as in Toc H); ''s' here is 'is', joining the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is an alarm bell or signal, so the word means an alarm or warning.

clue.text: Write, as on parchment, end of letter kept by inverted *letter-writer

indicators.note: turned upside down, so the back half of the name comes to the front
an end is the very last position, so only the closing character is kept
something kept by another is held inside it

blocks.note: Mr Collins of Pride and Prejudice, the starred theme, is famous for his pompous letters
the plain word, before the hyphenated one

explanation.surface: A letter-writer turned upside down keeps the end of his letter while writing on parchment.
explanation.walkthrough: Starred clues are Pride and Prejudice characters. COLL and INS swap places to give INSCOLL, and the R goes in after INSC.
explanation.definitionFit: To inscroll is an old verb for writing something on a scroll, the parchment roll.

clue.text: Leave thread on London street

blocks.note: first meaning: to leave someone stuck and helpless
second meaning: a single fibre or filament
third meaning: a famous thoroughfare in the West End

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a thread lying on a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: This is in fact three meanings: the Strand is a famous thoroughfare running from Trafalgar Square towards the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: To strand someone is to abandon them, a strand is a single fibre, and the Strand is the street.

clue.text: People putting to use a piano tool

blocks.note: taken as written
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
pliers are a gripping tool

explanation.surface: Workers using a tool on a piano, perhaps a tuner at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano tool' reads as one thing, a tuning lever; split it into the musical abbreviation and a separate tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Appliers are those who apply something, and to apply is to put to use.

clue.text: Colour for axe said to be axed from carpet fixers

indicators.note: said means spoken, so we want letters that sound like the word
axing something cuts it out, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: tin tacks are the short nails used to fix carpets
this spelling is pronounced the same as the tool

explanation.surface: A colour choice for a chopping tool, with something to be cut from the carpet fitters' kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell the sound of 'axe' as ACKS and cut it from TINTACKS, leaving TINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint is a shade or hue, a slight variety of colour.

clue.text: Frost report in verse?

indicators.note: a report is what is heard, so we want a word that sounds like another

blocks.note: verse is written in rhyme

explanation.surface: A request for a weather report on frost written in verse, or a nod to the poet Robert Frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost' looks like the poet Robert Frost, who wrote in verse; it is just the icy coating, and the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Rime is hoar frost, the white ice crystals that form on cold surfaces from freezing fog.

clue.text: Accustomed to being exploited

blocks.note: first meaning: familiar with
second meaning: taken advantage of

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about getting used to exploitation; the break comes after 'to', which belongs to the first meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: One is used to a thing when familiar with it, and someone who has been taken advantage of feels used.

clue.text: Cad caught in painting reversing vehicle

indicators.note: something reversing goes backwards, so its letters run the other way
a thing caught in another is trapped inside it

blocks.note: painting is an art
an oik is a boorish lout, British slang

explanation.surface: A scoundrel is spotted in a painting of a vehicle backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversing vehicle' seems to belong together, but 'reversing' turns the painting round and 'vehicle' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a Russian carriage or sleigh pulled by three horses abreast, so a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Girl who drowned without work caught with the sun

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: Ophelia drowns in Shakespeare's Hamlet
op, short for opus, is a work
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A girl drowned while out of work, caught along with the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: OP for opus is the musical work number; take it from the front of Ophelia.
explanation.definitionFit: Heliac means relating to the sun, used of a star rising or setting at the same time as the sun.

clue.text: Remove tied head covering from a good, clean Parisian

blocks.note: un is French for a
bon is French for good
net is French for clean
qualifies all three words before it: each goes into French

explanation.surface: Taking the hat off a smart, clean-cut Parisian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' tells us all three small words are to be put into French.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonnet is a hat tied under the chin, so to unbonnet is to take that hat off.

clue.text: *Clerk to 9's grandfather with letter to Greek speakers

blocks.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
we speak with our lips

explanation.surface: A clerk from the Bennet family past, speaking Greek letters to anyone who will listen.
explanation.walkthrough: Starred clues are Pride and Prejudice characters, and 9 is Elizabeth Bennet in the setter's numbering. 'Greek speakers' looks like people; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: In the novel Mr Philips was clerk to Elizabeth's maternal grandfather, a lawyer, and married his daughter.

clue.text: Bird, part of the overheads of Saturn?

definitions.text: part of the overheads of Saturn?

blocks.note: first meaning: a large flightless South American bird

blocks.clueFragment: part of the overheads of Saturn?
blocks.note: second meaning: one of the moons orbiting the planet

explanation.walkthrough: 'Overheads' sounds like business costs; here it is things overhead in the sky, and the moon is one of them. The question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is an ostrich-like bird, and Rhea is the second largest moon of the planet Saturn.

clue.text: Setter and solver abroad, in a sense

blocks.note: first meaning: French for we, the pair of us in a foreign language
second meaning: common sense, gumption

explanation.surface: The setter and the solver find themselves together overseas, in one sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter and solver together make 'we', and 'abroad' asks for it in French.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English nous means practical intelligence or good judgement, borrowed from the Greek word for mind.

clue.text: *9's friend dressed cot with tulle in coaches

indicators.note: to dress material is to work it into shape, so the letters are rearranged
put in means placed inside, so these letters go within the others

blocks.note: a chara is short for charabanc, an old motor coach
taken as written, the two words joined

explanation.surface: A friend has dressed a baby's cot in tulle while travelling by coach.
explanation.walkthrough: Starred clues are Pride and Prejudice characters, and 9 is Elizabeth Bennet. 'Coaches' looks like the verb; it is the plural of chara, and the coaches split to take the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte Lucas is Elizabeth Bennet's close friend in the novel, who marries the absurd Mr Collins.

clue.text: Death to the Roman emperor was from pacified orphaned backer

definitions.text: Death to the Roman emperor was
definitions.note: the answer completes this sentence as an adjective

indicators.note: an orphan has lost a parent, so the word for father is taken out
something going back runs the other way

blocks.note: taken as written
pa, father, is the parent the word loses

explanation.surface: A historical note on how death treated a Roman emperor, set against a placated orphan's sponsor.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman emperors were declared gods after death. 'Backer' looks like a supporter but just means run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Deific means making divine, and for an emperor death brought official deification by the Senate.

clue.text: Hornbeam, say, for court in Bordeaux region (no extremes)

indicators.note: without its extremes a word loses its two ends
one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: the Gironde is the French department round Bordeaux
to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: Hornbeam wood chosen to build a courtroom somewhere in the Bordeaux wine region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a law court; here it is the verb to woo, put inside IROND.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironwood is a name for various very hard timbers, and the hornbeam is one tree called that.

clue.text: Drape juniper with this to produce novel that is mythological

indicators.note: producing something new means making it out of the parts, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the novel of the starred theme
taken as written; these letters are the ones taken out of the title
stands for the answer itself, whose letters complete the title

explanation.surface: Instructions to drape juniper sprigs over something mythological to create a fresh effect.
explanation.walkthrough: This works backwards: drape juniper plus the answer rearrange to PRIDE AND PREJUDICE, the 'novel' of the theme. Take those letters away and EDDIC is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddic describes the Edda, the Old Norse collections of poems and stories about gods and heroes.

clue.text: Haunt of Apollo, a lost theatre

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
the Adelphi is a theatre on London's Strand

explanation.surface: Apollo's favourite spot was once a theatre, now gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The Adelphi is a long-running West End theatre; drop its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphi in Greece was the sanctuary of Apollo and home of his famous oracle.

clue.text: Eccentric flower for motorist

blocks.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person
a river flows, so it is a flower in crossword terms

explanation.surface: An odd bloom chosen as a gift for a driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' wants to be a bloom; read it as 'flow-er', something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist is someone who drives a motor car, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Composer gets a coin, a sovereign

blocks.note: the franc was the French coin before the euro
K is the abbreviation for king, a sovereign

explanation.surface: A composer is paid a coin, and a gold one at that.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is also an old British gold coin, which keeps the money theme going; here it means a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: César Franck was a Belgian-born composer and organist working in Paris.

clue.text: *Colonel in favour of canonising the Queen?

blocks.note: to be for something is to favour it
canonising makes a saint, abbreviated ST
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: An army officer who backs making the monarch a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: Starred clues are Pride and Prejudice characters. Canonising the Queen puts the saint's abbreviation in front of her royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonel Forster commands the militia regiment in the novel and takes Lydia Bennet to Brighton.

clue.text: Sort of word with somewhat abbreviated backing

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the next word is used
backing means moving backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the letters sit inside the word, after the first two

explanation.surface: Grammar talk about a kind of word that comes with a shortened support.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden backwards in 'abbreviated'; the definition is fair as a verb is one of the parts of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb is one of the grammatical classes into which words are divided, a doing or being word.

clue.text: Phone call saying it's a circular cutter

blocks.note: to give someone a buzz is to ring them
a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: A caller explains on the phone that the tool is a round blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saying' looks like part of the phone call; it is the noun meaning a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzz saw is a power saw with a spinning round blade, chiefly the American term for a circular saw.

clue.text: See 15
*9's sister or *6's aunt finds beast (female) in the East

blocks.note: a cat is a beast
her is the female pronoun
taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A relative discovers a female animal out in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: Starred clues are Pride and Prejudice characters: 9 is Elizabeth Bennet and 6 is Darcy. 'In' looks like a container signal but is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth's younger sister Catherine is known as Kitty, and Darcy's aunt is Lady Catherine de Bourgh.

clue.text: Victorian philanthropist giving backword in number by dramatist

indicators.note: the first half of this coinage says go back, so the second half is turned round
one thing in another is put inside it

blocks.note: the second half of the printed word, taken as written
L is fifty in Roman numerals
Joe Orton, the 1960s English playwright

explanation.surface: A Victorian do-gooder writes words backwards into a number by a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backword' is one printed word made of two parts: the signal and the word it turns. The dramatist's name opens up after OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Montagu Corry, Lord Rowton, founded the Rowton Houses, cheap decent lodgings for working men in London.

clue.text: *The baddie with joint on the burner

blocks.note: the wick is the part of a candle or lamp that burns
a ham is a joint of meat

explanation.surface: A villain with a joint of meat cooking on the stove.
explanation.walkthrough: Starred clues are Pride and Prejudice characters. 'Joint on the burner' reads as cooking, but 'on' just places one piece next to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: George Wickham is the novel's charming scoundrel, who slanders Darcy and elopes with Lydia Bennet.

clue.text: Picnic scene with no alternative must excel

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: a picnic is an outdoor scene
or is the word that offers an alternative

explanation.surface: A picnic with no other choice of setting has to be the best one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative' looks like a noun meaning option; it is the little word that introduces one.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo is to surpass, which is to excel over others; both are verbs.

clue.text: *She embodied the latter, being briefly divisible into two

blocks.note: one short form of the name, as Mr Collins and others call her
a second short form; the full name splits cleanly into the two

explanation.surface: A woman who stood for the second of two qualities, and whose name could be cut into halves.
explanation.walkthrough: The latter of Pride and Prejudice is prejudice, which the heroine embodies as Darcy does pride. Her name breaks into two familiar short forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Bennet, the heroine of the novel, forms a hasty prejudice against Darcy that she must overcome.

clue.text: Chinese philosopher from American city and Australian island

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles
Oz is the informal name for Australia
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A Chinese thinker who hails from somewhere in America and an island off Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Australian island' reads as one place; it splits into two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Laozi, also spelt Lao-tzu, is the traditional founder of Taoism and author of the Tao Te Ching.

clue.text: *6's friend in Yorkshire

blocks.note: first meaning: Darcy's amiable friend in Pride and Prejudice
second meaning: a town near Bradford in West Yorkshire

explanation.walkthrough: 6 is Darcy in the setter's numbering. The surface puts the friend in Yorkshire; the county clause is a separate meaning, a place found there.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Bingley is Darcy's wealthy, good-natured friend, and Bingley is also a West Yorkshire mill town.

clue.text: *32's brother-in-law and Ruth's bastard

indicators.note: a bastard form is a corrupted or impure one, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written, the possessive's s included

explanation.surface: Gossip about a brother-in-law and the illegitimate child of a woman called Ruth.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's own number points at the character linked by marriage; 'bastard' reads as an insult or a child, but works as an adjective meaning corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Hurst, married to Bingley's sister Louisa, is Bingley's indolent brother-in-law in the novel.

clue.text: Beast gets round censor

blocks.note: a cat is a beast
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An animal manages to evade the censor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets round' sounds like dodging; 'gets' only joins, and 'round' is the ring-shaped letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Elder held the Roman office of censor and became famous as Cato the Censor.

clue.text: Fast bowler's extract from Anglo-French dictionary?

blocks.note: first meaning: a cricket bowler who makes the ball deviate off its stitched seam
second meaning: an entry giving an English word with its French translation, the ocean in both languages

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful definition: an English-French dictionary pairs 'sea' with 'mer'. The question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a seamer is a fast or medium-pace bowler relying on movement off the seam of the ball.

clue.text: The sea in Macbeth

blocks.note: first meaning: an Antarctic sea named after the explorer James Clark
second meaning: a Scottish thane who appears in Shakespeare's play

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a phrase from the play, perhaps the 'multitudinous seas'; the two halves are separate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ross Sea is a bay of the Southern Ocean, and Ross is a Scottish nobleman in Macbeth.

clue.text: Bearing in 47 as 9 to Mrs 24

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: points at the clue 'Agreeable resort' in the setter's numbering
east is a compass bearing, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A family relationship described with numbered cross-references, like a genealogy puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers are the setter's own, not this grid's: 47 is the 'Agreeable resort' answer, 9 is Elizabeth Bennet and Mrs 24 her aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth is the daughter of Mrs Bennet's sibling, so she stands as niece to her aunts in the novel.

clue.text: Result of coup is an extra run

blocks.note: first meaning: the toppling of a government
second meaning: in cricket, a run scored when a fielder's throw goes past the stumps

explanation.surface: A coup ends with the plotters making an extra dash for it.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, if a return throw misses the stumps and nobody stops it, the batsmen can take additional runs, called overthrows.
explanation.definitionFit: A successful coup brings the downfall of a regime, and in cricket the word names a bonus run from a wild throw.

clue.text: *4 17's father gets one to replace energy in river in Thailand

indicators.note: replacing means one letter takes the place of another
something in another is put inside it

blocks.note: the Irwell is the river flowing through Manchester
I is the Roman numeral one
E, the physics symbol for energy, is the letter swapped out
Siam is the former name of Thailand

explanation.surface: A father takes someone along to stand in for the power on a Thai river.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 17 is Charlotte Lucas in the setter's numbering. Swap the E of the Manchester river for I and put the result inside Thailand's old name after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir William Lucas, a knighted former tradesman, is Charlotte's father and the Bennets' neighbour in the novel.

clue.text: *Heard sound of bustle

indicators.note: something heard reaches us by ear, so the name meant here is judged by how it is spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: bustle is said like Bussell, and the ballerina Darcey Bussell has a first name pronounced like the hero's surname

explanation.surface: Someone hears the noise of a busy crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The asterisk marks a character from the novel, which is the definition. Darcey Bussell was a famous British ballerina: bustle stands for her surname by sound, and her first name, heard, is the hero's.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitzwilliam Darcy is the proud hero of Pride and Prejudice who eventually marries Elizabeth Bennet.

clue.text: I cover up a chap who is industrious

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters read from the bottom

blocks.note: taken as written
a lid is a cover
a gent is a gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to covering up for a hard-working man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover up' reads as concealing; 'up' instead turns the first two pieces over, so both the I and the cover are reversed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligent means showing steady careful effort, which is what an industrious person shows.

clue.text: Impressive collection backed by chap with Australian horse

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: an array is an impressive display or collection
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A fine collection supported by a man who owns a horse from Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed by' reads as supported by; 'backed' turns the collection round and 'by' sets the chap after it. YARRA is also a Melbourne river, a happy accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarraman is an Australian word for a horse, probably from an Aboriginal language.

clue.text: Some of many with wind or water

indicators.note: only some of a thing means part of it is left off

blocks.note: a million is a great many

explanation.surface: Some of the many things powered by wind or water.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works by attachment: put wind or water in front and you get a windmill or watermill.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill grinds grain using power from a source, so the word forms windmill and watermill.

clue.text: Catch fish - what with? Not radio

blocks.note: to land a fish is to bring it out of the water
the answer to the question: a fishing line

explanation.surface: An angler asks what to catch fish with, and is told not to use a radio.
explanation.walkthrough: The question 'what with?' asks for the tackle you catch with.
explanation.definitionFit: A landline is a telephone connection by fixed cable rather than by wireless or mobile signal.

clue.text: A pretended laryngitis?

blocks.note: taken as written
phony means fake, put on

explanation.surface: Someone fakes a sore throat to get out of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that laryngitis is only one possible cause of the condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphony, or aphonia, is loss of the voice, which laryngitis typically produces.

clue.text: Say 52s (say) when we get our money

blocks.note: surface reading: a cryptic instruction to say something aloud, with an unexplained clue number
setter's reading: 52 is the 'Frost report in verse' answer in the setter's numbering, so spoken it means verses that chime, and both words of the answer chime with the word say

explanation.surface: A cryptic instruction followed by a plain question of when wages arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers are the setter's own: 52 is RIME, which said aloud is rhyme. Both PAY and DAY rhyme with 'say', so they are 'say rhymes', and together they make the day wages come in.
explanation.definitionFit: Payday is the regular date on which employers hand over wages or salary to staff.

clue.text: Sound of reproach in Hampshire

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: odium is the disgrace or reproach heaped on someone

explanation.surface: A disapproving tut heard somewhere in Hampshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county in southern England; the definition 'in Hampshire' is a place found there.
explanation.definitionFit: Odiham is a small town in Hampshire, home to an RAF helicopter base.

clue.text: Put your name down - put it for Flynn's right

indicators.note: to put one thing for another is to make it stand in its place

blocks.note: Errol Flynn, the swashbuckling film star
R, short for right, is the letter swapped out

explanation.surface: Sign up, and swap your name for the film star's legal claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' means the name just mentioned, abbreviated N, which goes in place of the first R in the actor's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to sign up for something, which you do by putting your name on a list.

clue.text: Grass on **9's sisters

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for cannabis
second meaning: two of Elizabeth Bennet's sisters, one starred light per sister

explanation.surface: Informing on Elizabeth's siblings, as a grass is a police informer.
explanation.walkthrough: The double star marks two characters; 9 is Elizabeth in the setter's numbering. 'Grass' looks like a verb meaning inform on, as 'on' supports.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Jane is slang for marijuana, and Mary and Jane are two of the five Bennet sisters.

clue.text: Will purposefully signified nothing

blocks.note: to signify is to mean
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A will that was drawn up with purpose turned out to mean nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a legal document; it is the verb of intention.
explanation.definitionFit: If I mean to do something, I intend to do it, so I will do it on purpose.

clue.text: They say Scotsman and German like the Daffodils' company

indicators.note: what people say is spoken, so we want a word that sounds like these

blocks.note: a Jock is a Scotsman, and und is German for and

explanation.surface: A Scot and a German, said to be as cheerful as Wordsworth's daffodils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And German' means the German word for 'and'. Jock is a British nickname for a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth's poem on daffodils says 'A poet could not but be gay, In such a jocund company', jocund meaning merry.

clue.text: Like Croesus, with *9's sister's name

blocks.note: the youngest Bennet sister, who elopes with Wickham
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: As rich as Croesus, and carrying the name of Elizabeth's sister.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the starred character supplies wordplay rather than the definition; 9 is Elizabeth Bennet.
explanation.definitionFit: Croesus was the fabulously rich king of Lydia in Asia Minor, so he was Lydian by nationality.

clue.text: Agreeable resort

blocks.note: first meaning: pleasant
second meaning: the city on the French Riviera

explanation.walkthrough: The capital letter of the place disappears at the start of the grid entry, so the adjective and the city share a spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means pleasant, and the Riviera city is a famous seaside holiday destination.

clue.text: *6 are going out first

definitions.note: the answer is Darcy's sister, whose full name includes the surname 6

indicators.note: going out of their places, the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; the word serves as fodder and as half the signal
A is the first letter, as in A1 or A-grade

explanation.surface: Several Darcys are setting out first.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is Darcy in the setter's numbering, so the answer is a first name to go with that surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgiana Darcy is Mr Darcy's shy younger sister, whom Wickham once tried to elope with.

clue.text: Clothes to be changed?

definitions.note: a cryptic hint at the thing a driver changes

blocks.note: first meaning: informal for clothing
second meaning: what a driver shifts while driving

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as laundry ready for changing into; the question mark marks the hop to motoring, where you change up or down.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for clothing, and in a car you change from one toothed ratio to another.

clue.text: Like some fish? Cut top of mat to go under it

indicators.note: cutting the top off removes the first letter of a down entry

blocks.note: a doily is a small lace mat put under a cake or plate

explanation.surface: Fish served on a plate, with instructions to trim a mat to sit underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' refers back to the fish on its plate, giving a mat that goes under food.
explanation.definitionFit: Oily fish such as mackerel, herring and sardines have oil throughout their flesh.

clue.text: Left to be devoured by fish, which isn't friendly

indicators.note: something devoured goes inside the eater

blocks.note: the cod is a fish
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Something abandoned to be eaten by an unfriendly fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a past tense, abandoned; it is the abbreviation.

clue.text: Cricket captain's part in declaration

indicators.note: a part found in a word is a run of its letters

blocks.note: the letters sit in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A cricket captain's role in declaring an innings closed.
explanation.walkthrough: A declaration in cricket is a captain ending his side's innings early, so the surface is all cricket. Brian Lara captained the West Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Lara, the record-breaking West Indian batsman, was captain of the West Indies team.

clue.text: Film maker's reduced place in series

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: a chain is a series of linked things
PL is the shortened form of place

explanation.surface: A film director finds his place in a franchise shrinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' means abbreviated here, not demoted.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin wrote, directed and starred in his own films, so he was a film maker.
